archetypes.name: git-commit-scoping-contract
archetypes.rationale: FINDING_2's staged-carryover fix depends on git-commit.sh --only --pathspec-from-file behaving exactly as the plan claims; if the script re-stages from the pathspec rather than restricting the existing index, or does not forward --only to git commit, the entire staged-carryover prevention is silently a no-op.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan's FINDING_2 fix claims that passing `--only --pathspec-from-file "$stage_manifest"` to `scripts/git-commit.sh` prevents pre-staged outside-manifest carryover from entering the round commit, because the script 'stages from the pathspec file before `git commit --only --pathspec-from-file=…`'. Read `scripts/git-commit.sh` in full and verify: (1) whether `--only` is actually forwarded to the underlying `git commit` invocation, (2) whether the script re-stages from the pathspec file (overwriting prior index state) or merely restricts what is committed from the existing index, and (3) whether the script handles an empty or missing pathspec file gracefully rather than committing everything. If the script's behavior diverges from the plan's description, the staged-carryover orchestrator test case (FINDING_2 assertion: `other.txt` absent from `git show HEAD`) would still pass if the test fixture never pre-stages carryover — flag whether the fixture in section B/C actually creates a pre-staged state that would expose a broken implementation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: snapshot-diff-parity
archetypes.rationale: path_is_pre_coder_carryover relies on git diff output matching the stored snapshot byte-for-byte; if snapshot_pre_coder_tracked_state uses different diff flags, context lines, or binary handling than the predicate's reconstruction, genuinely unchanged carryover files will fail the cmp check and the guard will still fire — reproducing the original bug.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan introduces `path_is_pre_coder_carryover` which validates carryover by comparing `git diff "$pre_head" -- "$path"` output against the stored patch file in `pre-coder-path-diffs/`. Read the existing `snapshot_pre_coder_tracked_state` function in `skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh` and verify that the `git diff` invocation used to create each snapshot file uses identical flags, context-line count, and binary-file handling as the predicate's reconstruction call — any flag mismatch (e.g. `--unified=N`, `--binary`, `--no-renames`) would cause the `cmp -s` check to fail for unchanged files. Also check whether the snapshot creation path trims or transforms diff output before writing (e.g. pipes through `sed` or strips headers), and whether the plan's proposed predicate code replicates the same transformation. Finally, confirm that the `pre_coder_path_diff_file` helper (used in both the existing `round_coder_delta_paths` and the proposed predicate) produces a safe filename for paths containing spaces or special characters, since `grep -Fxq` on `pre-coder-tracked-paths.txt` does exact-line matching. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
